headline: Rights body summons crime office chief after being denied access to ex-CJ Rana
dek: The bar association and cross-party leaders also accused the government of arbitrary rule a day after Rana's overnight detention.
body_markdown:
Nepal's human rights watchdog has summoned a senior police officer to explain why its own monitors were blocked from meeting former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana while he sat in custody. That escalation, a day after Rana's overnight detention, is sharper than the political outrage now surrounding the case.

The National Human Rights Commission, the NHRC, Nepal's constitutional rights watchdog, wrote to Senior Superintendent of Police Santosh Khadka on Monday, September 28. It ordered him to appear on Tuesday, September 29 at 11:30 am, NHRC spokesperson Dr Tikaram Pokharel told OnlineKhabar. A three member NHRC team had gone to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku on Sunday to check on Rana. Police made the team wait about 45 minutes at the gate, then turned it away without giving a reason, the Kathmandu Post reported.

Rana, whose tenure as Chief Justice ended amid a 2022 impeachment motion, was taken from his home in Maharajgunj at around 2 am on Sunday after roughly 90 minutes of persuasion by a police team, OnlineKhabar reported. Police initially described the action as a detention, OnlineKhabar reported. Hours later they revised the account, saying no arrest warrant had been sought and that Rana had instead been taken for his own protection after reports of a threat, according to SSP Khadka's comments to OnlineKhabar. Rana's brother, Prabhu Shumsher, said police told the family the threat came from Gen Z groups, though Rana himself had asked only for extra guards at home, OnlineKhabar reported. Police kept his phone in custody for nearly 12 hours, Ratopati reported.

That ambiguity, arrest or protection, matters to any reader in Nepal because it decides which legal safeguards applied to a former head of the judiciary, and by extension to any citizen police choose to remove from home at night.

## What the coverage missed

The Nepal Bar Association's Monday statement went further than most headlines captured. Beyond calling the detention contrary to the constitution and the rule of law, as Republica reported, the association's general secretary Kedar Prasad Koirala termed the episode "mysterious and suspicious" and said the block on NHRC access had deepened its concern, according to English Ratopati.

Rana's current troubles sit atop an unresolved public record. In 2022, 98 ruling coalition lawmakers filed a 21 point impeachment motion accusing him of promoting corruption in the judiciary and interfering in judicial appointments, Kathmandu Post reported at the time. The House of Representatives never voted on it before its term expired, and the Supreme Court has since closed the matter without ruling on the substance of the allegations, according to Nepalnews's account of how the impeachment saga ended.

Gen Z activist Miraj Dhungana wrote to the Home Minister on Monday, September 28, demanding public evidence that Rana had received threats from Gen Z groups, Nepal Press reported. Dhungana is not the only Gen Z activist to challenge the government's stated justification. A day earlier, on September 27, fellow activist Ajay Sodari had already asked authorities to make public the basis for any claimed threat from Gen Z groups, Nepal Press reported.

## What we still do not know

- What specific evidence led police to describe a security threat from Gen Z groups, and who is accused of making it. Only the Home Ministry and SSP Khadka can answer.
- Whether Rana was formally arrested or held without a warrant, and under what legal authority. Nepal Police's spokesperson and the Home Ministry's legal division could clarify.
- What SSP Khadka tells the NHRC on Tuesday about denying its team access. Only the commission and Khadka can say.

Cross-party criticism grew Monday outside the federal parliament building. Maoist Centre chair Pushpa Kamal Dahal called the stated security threat "merely an excuse" and said arresting prominent figures without cause could prove costly, Republica reported. RPP parliamentary leader Gyanendra Shahi accused the government of abusing state power to settle personal scores, DC Nepal reported. UML MP Kshitiz Thebe called the manner of Rana's pickup a mockery of law and procedure, OnlineKhabar reported. Rana's son, in a separate request, asked police for additional security at the family home, Setopati reported.

The NHRC hearing set for Tuesday, September 29 is the next fixed date on the calendar.

key_facts.fact: The National Human Rights Commission summoned SSP Santosh Khadka to appear Tuesday, September 29 at 11:30 am over Rana's detention.
An NHRC team was made to wait about 45 minutes at the gate of the Teku crime office before being turned away without meeting Rana.
The Nepal Bar Association said detaining and releasing citizens without sufficient grounds violates the constitution and the rule of law.
Police kept Rana's mobile phone in custody for nearly 12 hours after taking him from his Maharajgunj home.
98 ruling coalition lawmakers filed a 21 point impeachment motion against Rana in 2022 alleging corruption in the judiciary.
Maoist Centre chair Pushpa Kamal Dahal called the government's stated security threat merely an excuse and said arresting prominent figures without cause could prove costly.

social_hook: Nepal's rights commission has summoned a crime office chief for blocking its own monitors from meeting ex-Chief Justice Rana in custody.
take: The National Human Rights Commission's decision to summon SSP Santosh Khadka shows the commission is not satisfied with how police handled its own monitors' visit to see former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana. Police made the NHRC team wait 45 minutes at the gate of the Teku crime office, then turned it away without giving a reason, the Kathmandu Post reported. Police have also shifted their account of Rana's removal from home, first calling it a detention and later describing it as protective custody over an unnamed threat from Gen Z groups, OnlineKhabar reported. That threat has not been made public even after Gen Z activists demanded evidence, Nepal Press reported. Whether Rana was arrested or protected remains an open question that only SSP Khadka and the Home Ministry can answer, and Tuesday's hearing is the first chance to get a straight answer.

caption.hook: Police kept Nepal's human rights commission waiting 45 minutes at the gate, then sent its monitors away without seeing former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana.
caption.body: Former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana was taken from his Maharajgunj home at around 2 am on Sunday, September 27, OnlineKhabar reported. Police first described it as a detention, then said no arrest warrant existed and that Rana had been moved for his own protection after reports of a threat from Gen Z groups. Gen Z activists Ajay Sodari and Miraj Dhungana have publicly demanded the government make that evidence public, Nepal Press reported. The Nepal Bar Association called the episode mysterious and suspicious. When the National Human Rights Commission sent a team to check on Rana, police made them wait 45 minutes at the gate and turned them away. The commission has now summoned Senior Superintendent Santosh Khadka to appear Tuesday, September 29 at 11:30 am to explain the denial.
caption.trigger: Taken from home at 2 am with no warrant. Protection or detention?

angles.claim: The National Human Rights Commission's own monitoring team was blocked from meeting Rana in custody for roughly 45 minutes to an hour and turned away at the gate of the Teku crime office; the Commission has since summoned Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office chief SSP Santosh Khadka to explain why. This institutional escalation is absent from every candidate article's framing of the day, which centers only on party politicians and the Bar Association.
angles.why_it_matters: A constitutional watchdog formally objecting to police conduct and summoning a named senior officer is a harder, more consequential fact than politicians' quotes, and it independently corroborates due-process concerns without relying on any party's framing.

evidence.fact: SSP Santosh Khadka has been asked to explain why a National Human Rights Commission team was denied access to former chief justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana while he was in custody.
The team waited at the gate for around 45 minutes before returning after it was denied access to Rana, and the commission called the conduct contrary to its mandate.
The Criminal Investigation Office, Teku, denied entry to a team from the National Human Rights Commission that had gone to meet former Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher Rana.
The commission issued the summons after Khadka ignored a team from the commission that visited to assess the situation.

angles.claim: Rana himself was the subject of a formal 21-point impeachment motion filed by 98 ruling-party lawmakers in 2022, including charges of promoting corruption in the judiciary and interfering in judicial appointments; the motion was sent to a recommendation committee but the record shows no resolution was ever completed before his term ended. None of today's reaction coverage mentions this unresolved public record while amplifying the 'abuse of power' framing.
angles.why_it_matters: Readers weighing whether Rana is a victim of political persecution or a public official with an unresolved corruption record need both facts; omitting the 2022 impeachment history leaves only one side of a documented record.

evidence.fact: Nepal's ruling coalition lawmakers filed an impeachment motion against Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher JB Rana over allegations of corruption.
The recommendation committee registered the motion against Rana with 21 allegations including promoting corruption in the judiciary and failing to discharge his duties.
98 lawmakers from the ruling parties had made 21 allegations against Rana, including promoting corruption in the judiciary and interfering in the appointment of justices and judges.

angles.claim: Police accounts of the pickup are internally inconsistent with the 'arrest' framing dominating headlines: Ujyaalo Nepal reports police explicitly told Rana at the moment of pickup that he was not being formally arrested, and separate OnlineKhabar English reporting has senior officer Santosh Khadka repeatedly describing the action only as bringing Rana in for his own safety over a 'security threat,' never as an arrest.
angles.why_it_matters: Whether this was a lawful arrest, a warrantless detention, or protective custody determines what legal protections applied and what recourse Rana has; the coverage largely repeats 'arrest' without examining this gap in police's own words.

evidence.fact: जबराले आफूविरुद्ध कुनै पक्राउ पुर्जी भए-नभएको सोध्दा प्रहरी टोलीले उनलाई औपचारिक रूपमा गिरफ्तार नगरिएको तर सुरक्षाका लागि सुरक्षित स्थानमा लगिएको बताएको थियो।

SSP Khadka claimed Rana was brought in due to a 'security threat,' saying information had been received suggesting a possible physical attack on him overnight, and that he was brought in for his own safety.
Police have also not identified the specific security threat or the person or group believed to have posed it.

angles.claim: Miraj Dhungana is not the first Gen-Z activist to demand proof of the government's youth-movement threat claim: fellow activist Ajay Sodari publicly objected a day earlier, on September 27, saying no basis for any threat from Gen-Z had been shown and asking for the claim's evidence to be made public.
angles.why_it_matters: Framing this as one activist's isolated letter understates a building pattern of the youth movement pushing back on being blamed for an unverified threat, which is relevant to how the government's justification is being received by the constituency it names.

evidence.fact: जेनजी अभियन्ता अजय सोडारीले राणामाथि कुनै किसिमको धम्की वा सुरक्षा खतरा नरहेको भन्दै दाबीको आधार र प्रमाण सार्वजनिक गर्न माग गरे।

unanswered.question: What specific evidence or intelligence did police and the Home Ministry rely on to describe a 'security threat' from Gen-Z groups against Rana, and who is the alleged source of that threat?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Home Ministry spokesperson and SSP Santosh Khadka, Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office

unanswered.question: Was Rana formally arrested under an arrest warrant, or held in some form of custody without one, and what is the legal basis for either action?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Police spokesperson and the Home Ministry's legal division

unanswered.question: What did SSP Santosh Khadka tell the National Human Rights Commission when summoned to explain why its monitoring team was denied access to Rana?
unanswered.who_could_answer: National Human Rights Commission and SSP Santosh Khadka

unanswered.question: Is there any connection between the criminal complaint that reportedly triggered the Crime Branch's action and the unresolved 21-point corruption allegations from Rana's 2022 impeachment motion?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office and the parliamentary secretariat that held the 2022 impeachment file

investigation.summary: Nepal Wire can report today what the reaction round-ups leave out: the National Human Rights Commission was itself denied access to Rana in custody and has summoned the responsible SSP to explain, an institutional escalation independent of party politics. It can also supply record context missing from the 'persecuted ex-CJ' framing — Rana faced an unresolved 21-point corruption impeachment in 2022 — and flag that police's own words to Rana and to reporters describe this as safety custody, not an arrest, a distinction the current coverage glosses over.

ranking.reason: This is a real development since our September 27 arrest piece (s1). The Nepal Bar Association has issued a formal statement, opposition leaders across parties have gone on record, Ratopati reports the phone was seized for nearly 12 hours, and Miraj Dhungana has written to the Home Ministry demanding proof of the threat claim, all confirmed by separate outlets. Reach is 66 (hook 7, buried angle 6, emotion 6, friction 8, share identity 6, recognition 8, stakes 6), and the weakest weighted dimension is the buried angle, because Kathmandu Post already ran the opposition reaction.

Confirmed. This is a real development since our September 27 arrest piece (s1): the Nepal Bar Association statement on Monday, September 28, the on-record cross-party criticism, Ratopati's report of a phone seizure lasting nearly 12 hours and Miraj Dhungana's letter to the Home Ministry, each carried by a separate outlet. Reach is 66, and the weakest dimensions tie at 6: buried angle, emotion, share identity and stakes, with the buried angle hurt most because Kathmandu Post already ran the opposition reaction.

findings.passage: A three member commission team led by member Manoj Duwadi had gone to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku on Sunday to check on Rana.
findings.problem: No source in the article's own sources list or the investigation evidence names 'Manoj Duwadi.' The Kathmandu Post, OnlineKhabar, Khabarhub and Desh Sanchar evidence used to build this angle confirm the NHRC team was blocked but never name a team leader. This specific name appears to be invented or sourced from somewhere not disclosed, violating the 'nothing invented' rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Either find and cite the specific outlet that names Manoj Duwadi as team leader, or drop the name and simply say 'a three member NHRC team' without attributing an unverified name.

findings.passage: Police first called it a detention. Hours later they revised the account, saying no arrest warrant had been sought and that Rana had instead been taken for his own protection after reports of a threat, according to SSP Khadka's comments to Onlinekhabar and Republica.
findings.problem: Republica is not listed anywhere in the sources list as a source for SSP Khadka's protective custody comments. The only two Republica links in the sources list cover the Nepal Bar Association statement and Pushpa Kamal Dahal's quote, neither of which is about Khadka's account of the detention. Citing Republica here for content it is not on record credited with is a sourcing fabrication.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Republica attribution for Khadka's comments unless a specific Republica article carrying that quote is added to the sources list. Attribute only to OnlineKhabar if that is the actual source.

findings.passage: He was handed to his family roughly 12 hours later, and police kept his phone in custody for nearly 12 hours, Ratopati reported.
findings.problem: The Ratopati source in the sources list is used_for 'Phone seizure detail' only. The claim that Rana was 'handed to his family roughly 12 hours later' is not attributed to any source and reuses the same '12 hours' figure as the separately sourced phone detail, suggesting the release timing may have been inferred from the phone custody duration rather than independently confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the specific outlet and timestamp that reports when Rana was returned to his family, separate from the phone custody figure, or remove the release-timing claim if no source states it directly.

findings.passage: Police first called it a detention.
findings.problem: No named outlet is cited for the claim that police 'first called it a detention.' This is an unattributed characterization of police's initial framing, which the house style requires to be sourced like any other claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute this to whichever outlet first reported police calling the action a detention, or rephrase to avoid asserting an unsourced initial framing.

findings.passage: Miraj Dhungana is not the only Gen Z activist to challenge the government's stated justification.
findings.problem: This is the article's only mention of Miraj Dhungana, but the piece never states what Dhungana actually did (his letter to the Home Ministry demanding proof of the Gen Z threat claim). A reader with no prior knowledge cannot understand what is being referenced, failing the zero knowledge test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence explaining that Dhungana wrote to the Home Minister demanding public evidence of the claimed Gen Z threat, before saying he is not the only one to do so.

findings.passage: Rights body summons police chief after being denied access to ex-CJ Rana
findings.problem: Santosh Khadka is a Senior Superintendent of Police heading the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office, not Nepal's national police chief (the Inspector General of Police). Calling him 'police chief' in the headline risks readers believing the country's top police official was summoned.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a precise title such as 'crime office chief' or 'senior police officer' instead of the ambiguous 'police chief.'

findings.problem: The investigation surfaced a fourth strong angle, that Ujyaalo Nepal reported police telling Rana directly he was not being formally arrested when he asked for a warrant, distinguishing an arrest from protective custody in his own presence. This angle is only partially folded into the general body text and the specific Ujyaalo Nepal sourced detail is dropped, weakening the piece's strongest legal-status finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the specific detail that police told Rana in person he was not formally arrested, sourced to Ujyaalo Nepal, and add that outlet to the sources list.

findings.passage: (no image_headline, caption, or take fields present in the article object)
findings.problem: The article package supplied for review does not include the image_headline, caption, or take fields that the style guide and review process require for the card and Facebook post. Without these, the card headline cannot be checked for the mandatory status signal on an allegation, and the take cannot be checked against the body's facts before this piece goes to social distribution.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not publish or push to social until image_headline, caption, and take are drafted and each is checked against the body for unsupported claims, missing status signals, and adjectives the body cannot carry.

findings.passage: That escalation, a day after Rana's overnight detention, is sharper than the political outrage now surrounding the case.
findings.problem: This is the newsroom's own comparative editorial judgment about which storyline matters more, stated as fact in the lead rather than attributed. It is defensible as analysis but sits close to the line the style guide draws between reporting and asserting a conclusion in the newsroom's voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase to something like 'That escalation adds an institutional dimension the political reactions alone do not carry,' keeping the point but softening the unattributed ranking of importance.

findings.passage: Rana's brother, Prabhu Shumsher, said police told the family the threat came from Gen Z groups, though Rana himself had asked only for extra guards at home, OnlineKhabar reported... Rana's son separately asked police for additional security at the family home, Setopati reported.
findings.problem: Two different family members (brother and son) are described making closely related but separately sourced security requests within the same short passage, without clarifying whether these are the same request reported by two outlets or genuinely separate actions, risking reader confusion about the sequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify with a short phrase, such as noting the son's request came separately on Monday, to distinguish it clearly from the brother's earlier account of Rana's own request for guards.

red_team.summary: The body is generally well attributed and balances the government's protective custody framing against Gen Z activists' pushback and the Bar Association's objections, but it contains at least two serious sourcing problems: an unnamed team leader detail with no traceable source and a Republica citation for content Republica is not credited with reporting elsewhere in the sources list. The piece also reuses the same twelve hour figure for two different facts without separate sourcing, and never explains who Miraj Dhungana is or what he did before referencing him. Most critically for distribution, the image_headline, caption and take fields required for the card and Facebook post are entirely missing from this package, so the piece cannot be cleared for publication until those are drafted and checked against the same standards applied to the body.

responses.response: The sources list has no entry whose used_for field credits any outlet with naming a team leader for the NHRC visit, and none of the key_facts entries mention a name either. Under the nothing invented rule, a specific name that cannot be traced to a listed source must not appear in copy, even if it were accurate. This needs to be dropped or sourced.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'A three member NHRC team had gone to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku on Sunday to check on Rana.' Remove 'led by member Manoj Duwadi' unless a specific outlet naming him is added to the sources list.

responses.response: Both Republica links in the sources list are used_for the Bar Association statement and the Dahal quote, not for SSP Khadka's revised account. OnlineKhabar's two detention-timeline links are clearly used_for the protective custody account, so Republica should not ride along on that attribution without its own listed source.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'according to SSP Khadka's comments to OnlineKhabar' and remove 'and Republica' unless a Republica article carrying Khadka's own words is added to the sources list.

responses.response: The Ratopati source is listed only for the phone seizure detail. Reusing the same 'nearly 12 hours' figure for when Rana was returned to his family, without a distinct citation, reads as an inference dressed as a separately sourced fact.
responses.proposed_edit: Either find and cite the specific outlet reporting the family handover time, or cut the clause: 'and police kept his phone in custody for nearly 12 hours, Ratopati reported' stands alone without the unsupported release-timing claim.

responses.response: The sentence asserts police's initial framing as fact with no outlet named. The dek and lead already use 'detention' as the working description, which implies this was the early reporting language, but the specific claim that police used that word first needs its own attribution to survive scrutiny.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'Police initially described the action as a detention, OnlineKhabar reported.' citing the timeline piece already in the sources list (cholendra-rana-arrest-detain.html).

responses.response: The passage assumes the reader already knows what Dhungana did. The zero knowledge test fails here because his letter demanding proof of the Gen Z threat is never described before the sentence references 'the government's stated justification' he supposedly challenged.
responses.proposed_edit: Insert before the sentence: 'Gen Z activist Miraj Dhungana wrote to the Home Minister on Sunday demanding public evidence that Rana had received threats from Gen Z groups, Nepal Press reported.' Then keep the existing sentence about Sodari.

responses.response: Khadka is a Senior Superintendent of Police running a crime investigation office, not the Inspector General of Police who heads Nepal Police nationally. The headline's 'police chief' overstates his rank and could mislead readers about the scale of the NHRC's move.
responses.proposed_edit: Headline: 'Rights body summons crime office chief after being denied access to ex-CJ Rana'

responses.response: This is a suggestion to add a new angle from an outlet not currently in the sources list, not an error in what is written. The article already covers the arrest versus protective custody ambiguity through SSP Khadka's on record comments to OnlineKhabar, which is the core legal status question. Folding in one more outlet's phrasing of the same point is an enhancement, not a fix to a defect, and adding an uncross checked new source this late risks its own verification gap.
responses.proposed_edit: No change required for this version. If the Ujyaalo Nepal detail is independently verified in a follow up, it can be added to an update with the outlet listed as a source.

responses.response: House style requires image_headline and caption for every piece before it reaches social distribution, and the package as supplied has neither. That is a real gap even though it is a production step rather than a body text error.
responses.proposed_edit: Add before publish: image_headline (two lines, under 24 characters each, e.g. 'NHRC SUMMONS\nPOLICE OVER RANA') and a caption following the hook, body, trigger structure, both checked against the body for unsupported claims before the piece goes to social.

responses.response: House style explicitly tells writers to take a position when the facts support one rather than hedge. The sentence is analysis, not a disputed factual claim: an independent constitutional watchdog issuing a summons over blocked access is a documented, higher order institutional response than political statements, and the body substantiates this by detailing the summons before the political reactions. This is framing, not invention.
responses.proposed_edit: No change needed. If softened further, it could read: 'That escalation, a day after Rana's overnight detention, adds an institutional dimension the political reactions do not carry on their own.' but the original is defensible as written.

responses.response: The passage juxtaposes the brother's account of Rana asking for guards with the son's separate request for security without a clear time marker, which could read as one blurred episode rather than two distinct family statements from two outlets.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the son's sentence to: 'Rana's son separately asked police for additional security at the family home on Monday, Setopati reported.' adding the day to distinguish it from the brother's account of the Sunday incident.

defense.summary: Six findings expose real sourcing gaps: an unverified name (f1), a misattributed outlet (f2), a reused figure presented as independently sourced (f3), an unattributed characterization (f4), a reference to an unexplained activist (f5), and an imprecise rank in the headline (f6). All six are accepted with minimal fixes that preserve the reporting. The missing social fields (f8) and the family timeline clarity (f10) are also accepted as legitimate, low cost fixes. Two findings are contested: f7 asks for an additional angle from a new, uncross checked outlet when the existing sourcing already covers the arrest versus protective custody question, and f9 flags defensible editorial framing that the house style itself instructs writers to use rather than hedge.

rulings.note: No listed source names Manoj Duwadi. Under the nothing invented rule the name comes out unless an outlet naming him is added to the sources list.
Neither Republica link carries Khadka's protective custody account. Attribute to OnlineKhabar only.
Ratopati is listed only for the phone detail. The release timing reuses the same figure with no separate source.
The claim about police's initial framing needs a named outlet. The OnlineKhabar timeline piece is already listed.

Dhungana is referenced without explanation, which fails the zero knowledge test. The defence dated his letter to Sunday, but the Nepal Press URL is dated September 28, a Monday. The fix must use Monday.
Khadka is an SSP heading the Valley crime office, not the IGP. 'Police chief' in the headline overstates his rank.
This is an enhancement from an unlisted, unchecked outlet, not a defect. The arrest versus protection ambiguity is already covered through Khadka's on record account.
There is no image_headline, caption or take. The card and Facebook text cannot be checked or published. This blocks approval.
The house style asks writers to take a position when the facts support one. The summons is documented and is a higher order institutional act. This is framing, not an unsourced factual claim.
A day marker on the son's request cheaply separates it from the brother's account.

required_edits: Headline: replace with 'Rights body summons crime office chief after being denied access to ex-CJ Rana' to fix the rank. Source: OnlineKhabar English NHRC summons piece.

Body paragraph 2: change 'A three member commission team led by member Manoj Duwadi had gone' to 'A three member NHRC team had gone'. Only restore the name if an outlet naming him is added to the sources list.

Body paragraph 2: fix the attribution on the 45 minute wait so it names an outlet listed for that fact. key_facts credits Kathmandu Post while the body credits OnlineKhabar English. Use 'the Kathmandu Post and OnlineKhabar reported' only if both carry the detail. Otherwise use the one that does.

Body paragraph 2: add one sentence stating the reason police gave for denying the NHRC team access, attributed to the Kathmandu Post. The sources list credits the Post with 'reason for access denial'. If the Post reports that police gave no reason, say that instead. This supplies the subject's response required by the legal protection rules.

Body paragraph 3: change 'according to SSP Khadka's comments to Onlinekhabar and Republica' to 'according to SSP Khadka's comments to OnlineKhabar'.

Body paragraph 3: cut 'He was handed to his family roughly 12 hours later, and'. The sentence should read 'Police kept his phone in custody for nearly 12 hours, Ratopati reported.' Restore the release timing only with a separately listed source that states it.

Body, Gen Z paragraph: insert before the Dhungana sentence: 'Gen Z activist Miraj Dhungana wrote to the Home Minister on Monday, September 28, demanding public evidence that Rana had received threats from Gen Z groups, Nepal Press reported.' Do not say Sunday. Source: nepalpress.com/2026/09/28/768453.

Body, cross-party paragraph: change 'Rana's son separately asked police for additional security at the family home, Setopati reported.' to add 'on Monday' after 'family home'. Confirm the day against the Setopati item's timestamp. If the day cannot be confirmed, write 'in a separate request' instead.
Dek: change 'cross-party opposition leaders' to 'cross-party leaders'. No listed source establishes that the UML is in opposition.

Add image_headline in two lines, each 24 characters or fewer, with no colon, stating only verified actions. For example 'NHRC SUMMONS SSP KHADKA' and 'AFTER RANA ACCESS DENIED'. The summons and the denial are both documented by OnlineKhabar and the Kathmandu Post.

Add a caption. Hook: 'Police kept Nepal's human rights commission waiting 45 minutes at the gate, then sent its monitors away without seeing former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana.'
